funFacts: "Tabby" describes a coat pattern, not a breed -- the swirls, stripes, or spots can show up in almost any cat.
Most tabbies have a faint 'M' marking on their forehead, which some folklore ties to Mau, the Egyptian word for cat.
Tabby patterns come in four main types: classic (swirled), mackerel (striped), spotted, and ticked.
Siamese cats are famously vocal and will hold entire 'conversations' with their owners.
Their signature color points are heat-sensitive -- cooler areas like the ears, face, and tail run darker.
The breed traces back centuries to Siam (modern-day Thailand), where it was once kept by royalty.
Maine Coons are one of the largest domestic cat breeds, with males often topping 18 pounds.
Their tufted paws act like natural snowshoes, a trait suited to their cold New England origins.
Despite their size, they're known as 'gentle giants' with famously easygoing temperaments.
The breed's round face and dense, plush coat make it one of the most recognizable in the world.
It's believed to descend from cats brought to Britain by Roman traders nearly 2,000 years ago.
The Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland is widely thought to have been inspired by this breed.
